# Overview

## 

Based on the recommendations on the [nf-core/rnaseq](https://nf-co.re/rnaseq/latest/docs/usage/#reference-genome-options) and [STAR](https://physiology.med.cornell.edu/faculty/skrabanek/lab/angsd/lecture_notes/STARmanual.pdf) documentation we use the Ensembl assembly (`.fa.gz`) and annotations (`.gtf.gz`). As March 2025 the last Ensembl release is 113. The soft-masked version (`dna_sm`) was downloaded.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
cd /project/kplemon/RefGenomes/Homo_sapiens_GRCh38
VERSION=113
wget -L ftp://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-$VERSION/fasta/homo_sapiens/dna/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.dna_sm.primary_assembly.fa.gz
wget -L ftp://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-$VERSION/gtf/homo_sapiens/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.$VERSION.gtf.gz
```


## 

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Set up your R environment and read the GFF3 file. Adapt based on the GFF3 name and location
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

GENOMES_DIR <- here("inst/extdata/Ensembl")
GENOME_NAME <- "Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.113.gtf.gz"

library(rtracklayer)

# Import GTF file
gtf_data <- import(file.path(GENOMES_DIR, GENOME_NAME))

# Extract gene annotations
gene_anno <- data.frame(
  Geneid = mcols(gtf_data)$gene_id,
  gene = mcols(gtf_data)$gene_name,
  biotype = mcols(gtf_data)$gene_biotype
)
gene_anno <- gene_anno[!duplicated(gene_anno$Geneid), ]

# We save as a RDS object for later uses
saveRDS(gene_anno, file.path(GENOMES_DIR, "Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.113.rds"))
```
